Here’s a **comprehensive summary** of your client’s 12-week programme, integrating upper-body strength, body recomposition nutrition, cardio, climbing-specific prep, mobility, and a fun Saturday finisher. This plan is tailored for a 29-year-old recreational climber, post-right subacromial impingement, cleared for pain-free range and no overhead loading.

---

# 12-Week Climbing Strength & Conditioning Programme

---

## **1. Programme Structure**

**Phases:**  
- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):** Foundation & Activation  
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):** Strength Progression  
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):** Peak Strength & Climbing Prep

**Weekly Layout Example:**

| Day      | Focus                                   |
|----------|-----------------------------------------|
| Mon      | Upper Body Strength (Session A)         |
| Tue      | Cardio (steady-state or intervals)      |
| Wed      | Upper Body Strength (Session B)         |
| Thu      | Mobility or Rest                        |
| Fri      | Upper Body/Climbing Prep (Session C)    |
| Sat      | Saturday Finisher (Full Body, Fun)      |
| Sun      | Cardio or Active Recovery/Mobility      |

---

## **2. Strength & Climbing Programme**

### **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation & Activation**

- **Focus:** Pain-free range, scapular stability, basic push/pull, rotator cuff, grip.
- **Sessions:**  
  - **A:** Seated chest press, seated row, band pull-aparts, farmer’s carry  
  - **B:** Single-arm cable row, incline push-up, external rotation, wrist roller  
- **Volume:** 3x10–15 reps, moderate rest, light to moderate load

---

### **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength Progression**

- **Focus:** Increased load/volume, more unilateral/anti-rotation, climbing grip work.
- **Sessions:**  
  - **A:** DB floor press, seated cable row, band pull-aparts, farmer’s carry  
  - **B:** Single-arm landmine press, TRX row, Pallof press, wrist roller  
  - **C (optional):** Dead hangs (scapular engaged), plate pinch, climbing accessory  
- **Volume:** 4x8–12 reps, progressive overload

---

### **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak Strength & Climbing Prep**

- **Focus:** Max strength, power endurance, advanced grip/hangboard, climbing movement, peaking for trip.
- **Sessions:**  
  - **A:** DB floor press, chest-supported row, single-arm landmine press, heavy farmer’s carry  
  - **B:** Supersets (push-up/TRX row, cable row/Pallof), grip circuit  
  - **C:** Hangboard (7–10s hangs, 18–20mm edge, 6–8 sets), climbing movement drills, core  
- **Intensity:** Heavy loads (3–5 reps), reduced rest, high-intensity hangboard, taper in Week 12

---

## **3. Cardio (2x/Week)**

- **Goal:** Build aerobic base and climbing endurance
- **Types:**  
  - Steady-state (treadmill incline walk, bike, elliptical) 30–45 min  
  - Intervals (e.g., 1 min hard/2 min easy x 8–10 rounds)
- **Progression:** Increase duration/intensity over 12 weeks; simulate long climbing days in later phases

---

## **4. Climbing-Specific Prep (Weeks 9–12)**

- **Hangboard:**  
  - 1–2x/week, 7–10s hangs, 18–20mm edge, 6–8 sets, strict scapular control, pain-free only
  - Progress to repeaters or smaller edges if strong and pain-free
- **Movement Drills:**  
  - Footwork ladders, hip turns, flagging, easy traversing/bouldering (technique focus)
- **Core:**  
  - Plank with shoulder taps, dead bug, Pallof press

---

## **5. Mobility Routine (3–5x/Week)**

- **Shoulder/Scapular:** Scapular CARs, wall slides, pendulum swings, band dislocates
- **Thoracic:** Open books, quadruped T-spine rotations, foam roller extensions
- **Pec/Lat:** Doorway pec stretch, lat stretch on wall
- **Wrist/Forearm:** Flexor/extensor stretches, prayer stretch
- **Climbing-Specific:** Cat-cow, hip flexor stretch, deep squat hold

---

## **6. Saturday Finisher Day (Full Body, Fun)**

- **Circuit (2–3 rounds):**  
  - Sled push or farmer’s carry  
  - Goblet squat to box  
  - TRX/ring row  
  - Med ball slam (chest height)  
  - Bear crawl  
  - KB deadlift/RDL  
  - Battle ropes (chest height)  
  - Suitcase carry  
- **Optional:** Agility ladder, box step-ups, partner drills  
- **Cool-down:** Stretch, deep breathing

---

## **7. Nutrition Plan (Body Recomposition Focus)**

- **Calories:** Mild deficit (10–15% below maintenance; ~1700–1900 kcal/day, adjust as needed)
- **Macros:**  
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2g/kg BW/day  
  - Carbs: 3–5g/kg BW/day  
  - Fat: 0.8–1g/kg BW/day
- **Meals:** 3 main + 1–2 snacks, protein at every meal, carbs around workouts
- **Hydration:** 2–3L/day
- **Supplements:** Protein powder, creatine, vitamin D, fish oil (if needed)
- **Adjust:** Track progress, adjust intake every 2–3 weeks

---

## **8. Peaking & Taper (Week 12)**

- **Reduce volume by 30–40%, keep intensity high**
- **Extra rest and sleep**
- **Increase carbs slightly for glycogen**
- **Last hard session 3–4 days before trip**
- **Final days:** Only light mobility, easy cardio, short hangboard warm-ups

---

## **9. Safety & Progression**

- **No overhead loading or painful movements**
- **Strict scapular control on all upper-body and hangboard work**
- **Progress only if pain-free**
- **Monitor shoulder symptoms; regress if needed**
- **Regular check-ins and adjust as necessary**

---

## **10. Example Week (Phase 3)**

| Day      | Session/Focus                           |
|----------|----------------------------------------|
| Mon      | Upper Body Strength (A)                |
| Tue      | Cardio (steady-state, 40 min)          |
| Wed      | Power Endurance (B)                    |
| Thu      | Mobility or Rest                       |
| Fri      | Hangboard & Climbing Prep (C)          |
| Sat      | Saturday Finisher (Full Body, Fun)     |
| Sun      | Cardio (intervals, 30 min) or Mobility |

---

## Phase 1: Foundation & Activation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goals:**  
- Restore neuromuscular control  
- Build scapular stability  
- Begin bilateral and unilateral strength work  
- Emphasize pain-free movement and quality

**Weekly Structure:**  
- **Session A:** Horizontal Push + Pull, Scapular Stability  
- **Session B:** Unilateral Work, Rotator Cuff, Grip

**Session A**

---

## Cardio Integration for Climbing Endurance

### **Goals**
- Build aerobic base and muscular endurance for sustained climbing
- Support body recomposition and recovery
- Avoid shoulder aggravation (no overhead or jarring upper-body movements)

---

### **Weekly Cardio Structure**

**Frequency:** 2x/week  
**Duration:** 30–45 minutes per session  
**Type:** Low-impact, steady-state or interval-based, with minimal upper-body strain

---

### **Cardio Session Options**

#### **Option 1: Steady-State Endurance**

- **Treadmill incline walk** (4–6% incline, brisk pace)
- **Stationary bike** (upright or recumbent)
- **Elliptical** (with arms stationary or minimal use)
- **Rowing machine** (if pain-free and cleared by physio; otherwise, skip)

**Sample Session:**
- 5 min easy warm-up
- 25–35 min steady pace (RPE 6–7/10; able to hold a conversation)
- 5 min cool-down

#### **Option 2: Interval Endurance**

- **Bike Intervals:**  
  - 5 min warm-up  
  - 8 rounds: 1 min hard (RPE 8/10), 2 min easy (RPE 5/10)  
  - 5 min cool-down

- **Treadmill Intervals:**  
  - 5 min warm-up  
  - 10 rounds: 1 min brisk walk/jog, 1 min easy walk  
  - 5 min cool-down

---

### **Progression Over 12 Weeks**

**Weeks 1–4:**  
- 2x 30 min steady-state (bike, treadmill, elliptical)
- Focus on building duration and consistency

**Weeks 5–8:**  
- 1x 35–40 min steady-state

## Mobility Routine for Climbing & Shoulder Health

### **1. Shoulder & Scapular Mobility**

**A. Scapular CARs (Controlled Articular Rotations)**  
- *How:* Arm straight, make slow, controlled circles with the shoulder blade, both directions.  
- *Reps:* 5 each direction/side

**B. Shoulder Pendulum Swings**  
- *How:* Lean forward, let arm hang, gently swing in small circles.  
- *Reps:* 30 seconds/side

**C. Band Dislocates (to pain-free range)**  
- *How:* Hold a light resistance band wide, raise overhead and back as far as pain-free.  
- *Reps:* 10–15

**D. Scapular Wall Slides**  
- *How:* Back and arms against wall, slide arms up and down, keeping elbows and wrists in contact, only as high as pain-free.  
- *Reps:* 10

---

### **2. Thoracic Spine Mobility**

**A. Open Books**  
- *How:* Lie on side, knees bent, arms straight in front, rotate top arm open (like opening a book), follow with eyes.  
- *Reps:* 10/side

**B. Quadruped T-Spine Rotations**  
- *How:* On all fours, hand behind head, rotate elbow up toward ceiling, then down.  
- *Reps:* 10/side

**C. Foam Roller Thoracic Extensions**  
- *How:* Lie with upper back on foam roller, hands behind head, gently extend over roller.  
- *Reps:* 8–10

---

### **3. Pec & Lat Flexibility**

**A. Doorway Pec Stretch**  
- *How:* Forearm on doorframe, gently lean forward, feel stretch in chest.  
- *Hold:* 30 seconds/side

**B. Lat Stretch on Wall**  
- *How:* Hands on wall or bench, hips back, drop chest, feel stretch along lats.  
- *Hold:* 30 seconds

---

### **4. Wrist & Forearm Mobility**

**A. Wrist Flexor/Extensor Stretch**  
- *How:* Arm straight, palm up/down, gently pull fingers back with other hand.  
- *Hold:* 20–30 seconds each direction/side

**B. Prayer Stretch**  
- *How:* Palms together in front of chest, lower hands to feel stretch in wrists/forearms.  
- *Hold:* 30 seconds

---

### **5. Climbing-Specific Mobility**

**A. Cat-Cow (Spinal Flexion/Extension)**  
- *How:* On all fours, alternate arching and rounding back.  
- *Reps:* 10–15

**B. Hip Flexor Stretch**  
- *How:* Kneeling lunge, gently push hips forward, keep torso upright.  
- *Hold:* 30 seconds/side

**C. Deep Squat Hold**  
- *How:* Feet shoulder-width, squat as deep as comfortable, chest up, heels down.  
- *Hold:* 30–60 seconds

---

## **Sample 10-Minute Mobility Flow**

1. **Scapular CARs:** 5 each direction/side  
2. **Scapular Wall Slides:** 10  
3. **Open Books:** 10/side  
4. **Foam Roller Thoracic Extensions:** 8  
5. **Doorway Pec Stretch:** 30s/side  
6. **Lat Stretch on Wall:** 30s  
7. **Wrist Flexor/Extensor Stretch:** 20s each/side  
8. **Cat-Cow:** 10  
9. **Deep Squat Hold:** 30–60s

## **Guidelines**

- **Pain-free only:** Never push into pain, especially overhead.
- **Consistency:** 3–5x/week is ideal, especially after climbing or strength sessions.
- **Progression:** Gradually increase range as tolerated and cleared by physio.
- **Breathing:** Slow, deep breaths during all stretches and mobility work.

## **2. Strength & Climbing Programme**

### **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation & Activation**

- **Focus:** Pain-free range, scapular stability, basic push/pull, rotator cuff, grip.
- **Sessions:**  
  - **A:** Seated chest press, seated row, band pull-aparts, farmer’s carry  
  - **B:** Single-arm cable row, incline push-up, external rotation, wrist roller  
- **Volume:** 3x10–15 reps, moderate rest, light to moderate load

---

### **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength Progression**

- **Focus:** Increased load/volume, more unilateral/anti-rotation, climbing grip work.
- **Sessions:**  
  - **A:** DB floor press, seated cable row, band pull-aparts, farmer’s carry  
  - **B:** Single-arm landmine press, TRX row, Pallof press, wrist roller  
  - **C (optional):** Dead hangs (scapular engaged), plate pinch, climbing accessory  
- **Volume:** 4x8–12 reps, progressive overload

---

### **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak Strength & Climbing Prep**

- **Focus:** Max strength, power endurance, advanced grip/hangboard, climbing movement, peaking for trip.
- **Sessions:**  
  - **A:** DB floor press, chest-supported row, single-arm landmine press, heavy farmer’s carry  
  - **B:** Supersets (push-up/TRX row, cable row/Pallof), grip circuit  
  - **C:** Hangboard (7–10s hangs, 18–20mm edge, 6–8 sets), climbing movement drills, core  
- **Intensity:** Heavy loads (3–5 reps), reduced rest, high-intensity hangboard, taper in Week 12

---

## **3. Cardio (2x/Week)**

- **Goal:** Build aerobic base and climbing endurance
- **Types:**  
  - Steady-state (treadmill incline walk, bike, elliptical) 30–45 min  
  - Intervals (e.g., 1 min hard/2 min easy x 8–10 rounds)
- **Progression:** Increase duration/intensity over 12 weeks; simulate long climbing days in later phases

---

## **4. Climbing-Specific Prep (Weeks 9–12)**

- **Hangboard:**  
  - 1–2x/week, 7–10s hangs, 18–20mm edge, 6–8 sets, strict scapular control, pain-free only
  - Progress to repeaters or smaller edges if strong and pain-free
- **Movement Drills:**  
  - Footwork ladders, hip turns, flagging, easy traversing/bouldering (technique focus)
- **Core:**  
  - Plank with shoulder taps, dead bug, Pallof press

---

## **5. Mobility Routine (3–5x/Week)**

- **Shoulder/Scapular:** Scapular CARs, wall slides, pendulum swings, band dislocates
- **Thoracic:** Open books, quadruped T-spine rotations, foam roller extensions
- **Pec/Lat:** Doorway pec stretch, lat stretch on wall
- **Wrist/Forearm:** Flexor/extensor stretches, prayer stretch
- **Climbing-Specific:** Cat-cow, hip flexor stretch, deep squat hold

## **6. Saturday Finisher Day (Full Body, Fun)**

- **Circuit (2–3 rounds):**  
  - Sled push or farmer’s carry  
  - Goblet squat to box  
  - TRX/ring row  
  - Med ball slam (chest height)  
  - Bear crawl  
  - KB deadlift/RDL  
  - Battle ropes (chest height)  
  - Suitcase carry  
- **Optional:** Agility ladder, box step-ups, partner drills  
- **Cool-down:** Stretch, deep breathing

## **7. Nutrition Plan (Body Recomposition Focus)**

- **Calories:** Mild deficit (10–15% below maintenance; ~1700–1900 kcal/day, adjust as needed)
- **Macros:**  
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2g/kg BW/day  
  - Carbs: 3–5g/kg BW/day  
  - Fat: 0.8–1g/kg BW/day
- **Meals:** 3 main + 1–2 snacks, protein at every meal, carbs around workouts
- **Hydration:** 2–3L/day
- **Supplements:** Protein powder, creatine, vitamin D, fish oil (if needed)
- **Adjust:** Track progress, adjust intake every 2–3 weeks

---

## **8. Peaking & Taper (Week 12)**

- **Reduce volume by 30–40%, keep intensity high**
- **Extra rest and sleep**
- **Increase carbs slightly for glycogen**
- **Last hard session 3–4 days before trip**
- **Final days:** Only light mobility, easy cardio, short hangboard warm-ups

## **9. Safety & Progression**

- **No overhead loading or painful movements**
- **Strict scapular control on all upper-body and hangboard work**
- **Progress only if pain-free**
- **Monitor shoulder symptoms; regress if needed**
- **Regular check-ins and adjust as necessary**
